item.title: These are the apps and platforms Danes use, and you don’t. And these are the ones you should get rid of when you live in Denmark
item.description: Many very popular apps worldwide are barely known or used in Denmark. On the other hand, there are some “unique” apps and platforms here that exist only within Denmark’s borders. Messaging, sports, second-hand, car sharing: these are the apps you may not know, but that you need if you live here.

item.title: Denmark agrees with NATO countries on evacuation plan in the event of war
item.description: Denmark and nine other Northern European countries have agreed to develop a plan to evacuate citizens across borders in the event of war. The agreement includes Denmark, Poland, Germany, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Finland, Iceland, and Sweden. item.title: Denmark works on arranging flights for stranded citizens in the Middle East, but it can’t pay for them
item.description: The Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs is working to arrange extra flights to bring Danes home from the Middle East, where military attacks have left many travelers stranded. item.title: Social Democrats propose slower rise in retirement age, triggering a heated debate in the country
item.description: The Social Democrats have presented a major pension proposal that would slow the rise of the retirement age and expand the so called Arne pension scheme for early retirement, triggering a wide debate in Denmark. From 2045 onward, the party proposes that the retirement age should increase by half a year less than currently planned, […]

item.title: Glyptotek in Copenhagen to close for years for restoration work
item.description: Restoration works are expected to take between four and six years, the museum said in a press release Thursday. During that period, the museum will be closed to visitors.

item.title: Ukrainian refugees in Denmark say they are trapped in internships that violate labor laws
item.description: To stay in the country, many Ukrainian refugees have been stuck in internships performing dead-end tasks unrelated to their backgrounds with no path to permanent employment. In some situations, they say institutions exploited them, punished them if they protested, or turned a blind eye to their grievances.

item.title: Almost one in three voters prefer Mette Frederiksen as Prime Minister
item.description: A Voxmeter poll conducted for Ritzau shows that Mette Frederiksen remains the preferred choice for Danish Prime Minister, with 30.2% of respondents supporting her. Venstre’s chairman, Troels Lund Poulsen, ranks second with 9.1%, followed by Alex Vanopslagh at 8.2%. Lars Boje Mathiesen, who has also officially declared his candidacy, received 2.1% support.
